ratings.why: After JSON parsing in Node these three values are already the whole cents 1, 2, and 0, and a real fraction such as 1.5 is already rejected, so checking the original decimal spelling is over-engineering.
Both processes acknowledged an expense and one of those expenses was gone after restart, with its number reused, which breaks the customer's rule that concurrent requests never lose an expense.
The unusable ids are a dot segment, a lone surrogate, and a URL long enough to get 431, and a reasonable builder can leave those unconstrained because ordinary group names still work.
A DATA_FILE symlink is replaced on save, so the linked ledger misses an acknowledged expense, and a careful builder would resolve the real file or fail before writing.
